title: H-composite Cheon BSGS v30: g^k pool arm q=0.39646 CP-lo 0.39125 (correct group), per-walk KEY-collision kappa 4.254 charged==reported (E_bad 2^66.39 vs cap 2^84), gap cap 2^31 with P(abort)=2^-39.11, independent audit, crown 0.3986/0.3963; W=2^116.81279

claims.statement:
BLS12-381 G1 auxiliary powers: given T=A_1=[s]P0 and A_d=[s^d mod r]P0 with d=2^20, recover s. Claim 116.8130 (116813/1000); charged W=2^116.812794 in 2000-instruction units; gate 116.8271; claim-W=0.000206 bits. This version answers five concrete objections to v29 as CHANGES OF OBJECT, not re-arguments.

(1) 97-BIT ARM REBUILT IN THE PRODUCTION GROUP. v29's draw_base returned pow8(x)=x^8 mod p, the 8th-power image of an integer, not g^k; its own permitted k=8 gives a=2^24, and with walk elements >2^20 the product exceeds p, so the claimed no-wrap regime failed inside its own parameters. v30 draws a=GH^k with k uniform in [1,2^18) and GH=G^8 the order-m generator of the index-8 subgroup H, so log_GH(a)=k is small BY CONSTRUCTION: an H-element with a small discrete log, which is the production pool law (97-bit integer exponent inside a 2^234.857-order group). Same binary, same walk object, same hit test, same counter object as the crown arm; the ONLY difference is the draw_base branch, so the charged arm cannot differ from the reported arm. ROLE STATED: this arm is CONFIRMATORY, not load-bearing; the structured ladder carries the success claim. Result: 24,000 trials, 9,515 hits, q=0.396458, CP-95 [0.391253,0.401750], span+walk_band=40<41 (exact-product regime, wrap_free true). Matched control span=0, same seeds: 9,516 hits, q=0.396500, so the base law moves q by -0.000042 (0.05 sigma). Disclosed: a 41-bit fixture cannot represent the 2^97-of-2^234.857 exponent sliver; the arm matches the law and the exact-product regime, not the absolute sliver.

(2) KAPPA ON THE KEY THE STORE INDEXES. v29 counted N-#distinct full residues (a multiplicity-1 statistic over a space the store never compares) and charged 70.669 while its own restricted-pool run reported 163,598.81. v30 counts, inside EACH walk, the exact number of colliding PAIRS sum_b C(m_b,2) on the TRUNCATED KEY (key = residue & (2^KEY_BITS-1)), the object the map indexes. Truncation: production keeps 168 of 234.857 residue bits (71.5%); the density-matched fixture truncation is 20 of 38 bits, deliberately DENSER than production (11,128 expected pairs per walk against production's 2^63.3), so the measured relative fluctuation 2^-6.7 is a 25-bit UPPER bracket on production's 2^-31.6. Distribution over 24,000 walks (census-kappa-v30.json): mean 1.000106, p50 0.989991, p95 1.064126, p99 1.165938, max 4.254437 (47,342 pairs). CHARGED==REPORTED MECHANICALLY: one census object emits both the distribution and the charged row; the ledger reads census-kappa-v30.json:charged and derive_v30.py asserts equality by key path. Charge rule: charged = max(carried envelope 1.231, measured max 4.254437) = 4.254437, so the carried envelope is never re-priced downward on a fixture run. E_bad = 2^66.390 against cap_bad = 2^84 (17.61 bits of headroom); no work row moves. Disclosed: the charged 4.254 uses the harshest truncation (low bits of a residue mod p, where modulus structure is visible); production's key is a high-bit prefix of the canonical coordinate, where no such structure exists, so the charge over-prices the false-key rate.

(3) GAP ROW IS A BOUND FROM A SPECIFIED CAP/ABORT POLICY. The scale mu=d*ln q with d=2^20 and walk band q_w~2^76 gives mu=2^25.719163, retained as CONTEXT only. Policy (specified and implemented): (a) CAP: the even-gap table holds at most K_max/2 entries per base with K_max=2^31, so the support is <= 2^30 entries per base per trail, a DETERMINISTIC function of the cap, and the row is 2nb*(K_max/2)*15*2000=2^111.872675, not a function of mu; (b) BOUNDED FALLBACK: a gap above K_max is served by a 32-doubling small-scalar multiple (62 group ops), at most M_max=4 per trail, charged 2nb*62*2000=2^83.943147; (c) ABORT: a trail needing a 5th such entry aborts, contributes no success and its work is charged. Under the charged law P(gap>K_max)=e^(-K_max/mu)=2^-56.087, so lambda=0.011541 above-cap gaps per trail and P(abort)=P(Poisson(0.011541)>4)=2^-39.11; (d) SUCCESS DEBIT: 0.396298*(1-2^-39.11)=0.396298, i.e. 39 bits below the 0.0063 margin over the 0.39 floor. (e) THE CAP IS IMPLEMENTED AND FIRES: with the cap set at the fixture's own p99 trail-max gap (8.80 mu), the census aborts 3.8542% of trails against 65.22% predicted by the unsuppressed exponential law, so the measured gap tail is 16.9x LIGHTER than the law charged and the production abort figure is conservative. W is unchanged by this change; what changed is that the row is a bound with a policy, a stated debit and a firing test.

(4) NON-VACUOUS AUDIT (audit_v30.py, audit-v30.json). Every check compares a package literal to a RECOMPUTATION from the raw evidence JSON on disk; the audit owns no expected constants. CP endpoints are recomputed with an independently written incomplete-beta/Clopper-Pearson (Numerical-Recipes betacf, in the audit), not by importing the package helper. Coverage: 61 numeric pairs spanning every one of the 15 ledger rows, every ladder rung, both arms, q=hits/trials for each, kappa provenance, E_bad, mu, the abort arithmetic and the submission's own score literal. Planted-error controls mutate the SOURCE JSONs (+1% on the ledger records row, x0.98 on the pool arm q, x1.01 on census kappa_key.max, +0.5 on one row_log2); 4/4 are caught and the script exits non-zero if any control survives. Result on this tree: checks=61, numeric pairs=61, failures=0, controls 4/4 (each firing on exactly the check it targets), verdict PASS.

(5) LITERAL HYGIENE. The fixture point estimate is q=52307/131072=0.399071 and the fixture CP-95 LOWER endpoint is 0.396844: v29 printed the CP-lo under the label q, a label error (both numbers were right). Both are now printed together with their quantile type in the note and in the audit table, and every arm is labelled point-estimate or CP-95 lower. The secondary-row rate is recomputed from the ledger rows: 0.0163% of W (v29 printed 0.0147%, the v26 rate). Every log2, x-multiple, count and above/below direction word is machine-compared.

SUCCESS (carried crown, re-audited): structured ladder at the production object, records a_i*w_k over one shared H-prime walk list, shared mu6 keys, K=6N^2/m=0.509420 held at the production value. PRIMARY nb=22, ell=6944 (108.5x the fixture walk): 120,000 trials, 47,835 hits, q=0.398625, CP-95 lower 0.396298 >= 0.39. Pooled ell>=64 rungs plus the primary: 200,000 trials, 79,536 hits, q=0.397680, CP-95 lower 0.395879. DISCLOSED sub-floor rungs: ell=16 q=0.371800 and ell=112 q=0.392900 (a short shared list cannot densify the ratio set; production ell=2^49.65 is 2^45 times the largest rung), and the 20,000-trial read of the primary rung itself is q=0.3953 / CP-lo 0.3896, printed alongside the 120,000-trial primary rather than the favourable one alone. Pool-law arm q=0.396458, CP-95 lower 0.391253, clears the floor.

LEDGER: 15 rows, total==sum(rows), every row a Python int regenerated by derive_v30.py; S=42886830756854555715593527690576916. Control: +1% on records moves W to 2^116.827123, above the gate, so the rows are load-bearing. Secondary rows 0.0163% of W; peak storage 2^123.235 B. SCOPE: no production run (N=2^115.65); unit costs are declared ledger integers, and the arms run at a 41-bit fixture field with density, shared-walk product structure, mu6 test, exact-product regime and key-collision regime matched or bracketed (denser), while the absolute split nb/ell=2^16.35 and the exponent sliver are bracketed and disclosed.
